llcFilesWith: North Dakota Secretary of State (Trade Name Registration through the FirstStop portal)
soleProprietorFilesWith: North Dakota Secretary of State (the same statewide trade name registration applies to individuals and sole proprietors)
feeBasis: The Secretary of State fee to register a trade name through the FirstStop portal is $25 (§ 47-25-04 sets $25 for an original registration and $25 for an assignment).
renewalRule: A registration remains in force for five years from the date of the original registration and may be renewed within the ninety days before its expiration date by reregistering in the same manner as an original registration; the Secretary of State notifies the registrant at least ninety days before expiration (§ 47-25-04).
protectionNote: A North Dakota trade name carries more weight than most states' DBAs. Section 47-25-01(2) lets a person or organization that has registered a trade name institute a civil suit prohibiting any other person from using the name; § 47-25-03(1)(c) requires a trade name to be distinguishable in Secretary of State records from names already reserved or registered there; and § 10-32.1-11(1)(e)(4) folds registered trade names into the LLC name screen, so an active trade name blocks a later entity name that is not distinguishable from it.
searchNote: Registered trade names appear in the FirstStop business search alongside entity names.
notes: North Dakota registers trade names statewide with the Secretary of State under N.D.C.C. ch. 47-25, through the FirstStop portal ($25, five-year term, renewable in the ninety days before expiry). Registration is not optional: § 47-25-02 bars a person or organization from engaging in business in the state under a trade name until the name is registered. A North Dakota trade name also carries a right most states' DBAs do not, since § 47-25-01(2) lets the registrant sue to stop another person from using the name, and the trade name sits inside the entity-name distinguishability screen. Both LLCs and sole proprietors use it, and there is no publication requirement.
